# Contributing: Creating & Collaborating

## 🚀 Creating Your First Document

### Who Can Create Documents?

Most users can create documents in spaces and folders they have access to. Check with your team lead or administrator if you're unsure about your permissions.

### Creating a New Document

1. **Navigate** to the folder where you want to create the document
2. Click **"+ Create"** or **"New Document"** button (usually in the folder header)
3. Choose **document type**:
   - **Markdown**: Text with formatting (most common)
   - **Text**: Plain text file
   - **Other**: Depending on your installation
4. **Enter a title** for your document
5. Choose a **template** (optional—pre-filled structure to start from)
6. Click **Create**

### Editing Your Document

Once created, the document opens in edit mode:

1. **Title bar**: Shows your document name (click to rename)
2. **Tabs**: Choose view (Content, Blocks, Markdown, Visualize)
3. **Editor area**: Write your content
4. **Auto-save**: Changes save automatically (look for the "saved" indicator)
5. **Publish** (if required): Some organizations require explicit publish

### Formatting Your Content

The noobly Wiki supports **Markdown formatting**:

```markdown
# Heading 1
## Heading 2
### Heading 3

**Bold text**
*Italic text*
- Bullet list
- Another item
  - Nested item
1. Numbered list
2. Second item

> Quote or callout

[Link text](URL)
![Image alt](image-url)
```

### Adding Images & Files

1. Click **Insert Image** or drag an image into the editor
2. The image embeds inline in your document
3. For files: Create links to downloadable documents

### Blocks & Structured Content

The editor supports **blocks** (structured content components):

- **Code blocks**: Format code snippets
- **Tables**: Create data tables
- **Callouts**: Highlight important info
- **Video embeds**: Link to YouTube or other videos
- **Diagrams**: Create visual layouts
- **Related docs**: Link to other documents
- **Comments & Notes**: Add annotations

Use the **"+" button** in the editor to insert blocks.

## 💬 Commenting & Feedback

### Adding Comments to a Document

1. Open the document you want to comment on
2. Scroll to the **Comments section** at the bottom
3. Click **"Add Comment"**
4. Type your comment
5. Click **Post** or **Send**

Your comment is now visible to others who can see the document.

### Threaded Discussions

- **Reply to comments**: Click the reply button on any comment to respond
- **Tag people**: Type `@username` to notify someone
- **Mention documents**: Type to link another document
- **Edit your comment**: Click the edit icon (if available) to correct typos

### Comment Notifications

When someone comments:
- You'll see a notification (if enabled)
- Check the **Notifications panel** to see all comments
- Click the notification to jump to the comment

### Using Comments Effectively

Good comment practices:
- **Be specific**: Reference the exact section or idea
- **Be constructive**: Ask questions or suggest improvements
- **Tag the right people**: Use `@` to notify who should see this
- **Keep it brief**: Long feedback works better in a meeting
- **Resolve when done**: Mark resolved when feedback is addressed

---

## ✍️ Annotations & Highlights

### Annotating Text in a Document

Some documents support inline annotations:

1. **Select the text** you want to annotate
2. Click **Add Annotation** (or similar option)
3. Choose annotation type (comment, highlight, flag, etc.)
4. **Type your note** explaining why this is important
5. Click **Save**

The annotation stays with that text even if the document is edited.

### Viewing Others' Annotations

- **Highlighted sections** show what others have marked
- **Hover over highlights** to see their annotations
- **Annotation count** shows how many notes are on the document

### Editing & Removing Annotations

1. Click your annotation
2. Edit the text or click delete
3. Changes save automatically

---

## 🔗 Linking Documents Together

### Why Link Documents?

Linking shows relationships between documents:
- **Related concepts**: "API Design" links to "Security"
- **Follow-up reading**: A process links to detailed procedures
- **Context**: A decision document links to background research
- **Hierarchies**: A system overview links to component docs

### Linking From a Document

1. Open the document you want to add links from
2. Look for **"Link Documents"** or **"Related Documents"** section
3. Click **"+ Add Link"** or **"Link"**
4. **Search** for the document you want to link
5. **Select** the document from results
6. **Add optional label** (custom name for the link, if desired)
7. Click **Save**

### How Links Appear

Once linked, documents show:
- **"Linked Documents" section**: Shows related docs as cards
- **Backlinks**: Other documents linking to this one
- **Related**: Automatically suggested related documents

### Following Links

1. Find the **Linked Documents section** in a document
2. Click any **linked document card** to open it
3. You'll jump to that document (stays in your history)

### Creating a Link Network

Build knowledge networks by linking:
- Process → Detailed procedures
- Decision → Background research
- Overview → Component details
- Question → Answer document

Over time, this creates a web of knowledge.

## 🔄 Requesting Review

### Asking for Document Review

1. Add a comment mentioning your reviewer: `@alice Please review this design`
2. Or use a **"Request Review"** feature (if available):
   - Click **"Request Review"** in the document menu
   - Select reviewers
   - Add a note (optional)
   - Click **Send**

### Reviewer Workflow

Reviewers will:
1. Get a notification
2. Read the document
3. Add comments with feedback
4. Mark as "approved" or "needs changes"

### Responding to Feedback

1. Read the reviewer's comments
2. **Reply to each comment** with your response
3. Make changes to address feedback
4. Click **"Mark as Resolved"** when you've addressed it
5. Request another review if major changes were made

### Review Status

Some installations show review status:
- **Pending**: Awaiting review
- **Changes Requested**: Reviewer wants modifications
- **Approved**: Reviewer confirmed it's good

## 📝 Writing Good Contributions

### Document Structure

Good documents follow this pattern:

```markdown
# Title

## Overview
What is this document about? (1-2 paragraphs)

## Key Concepts
Explain the main ideas or terms.

## How It Works
Step-by-step or detailed explanation.

## Examples
Concrete examples or use cases.

## Related Documents
- [Document 1](#)
- [Document 2](#)

## FAQ
Common questions and answers.
```

### Writing Guidelines

- **Start with a summary**: readers should understand the topic in the first paragraph
- **Use headings**: break content into scannable sections
- **Add examples**: concepts are clearer with concrete examples
- **Keep it current**: update dates and version numbers
- **Use simple language**: technical docs should still be readable
- **Link to related content**: help readers learn more
- **Add visuals**: diagrams and screenshots aid understanding

### Citing Sources

When referencing other documents:
- **Link to them**: Use document links
- **Quote accurately**: Use quotation marks and credit the source
- **Provide context**: Explain why you're referencing something

## 👥 Collaborating on Documents

### Editing Together

If multiple people can edit:

1. **Note**: Someone else might be editing (watch for "editing by..." indicator)
2. **Real-time updates**: You'll see changes appear as others type
3. **Save often**: Changes auto-save, but monitor for conflicts
4. **Communicate**: Use comments to coordinate large edits

### Roles in Collaboration

- **Author**: Original creator
- **Contributor**: Adds to or edits the document
- **Reviewer**: Provides feedback before publishing
- **Maintainer**: Keeps it current over time

### Best Practices for Team Editing

1. **Divide work**: Agree on sections each person owns
2. **Use comments**: Discuss changes before making them
3. **Review changes**: Read what others added
4. **Resolve conflicts**: If two people edit the same section, discuss
5. **Keep history**: Document mentions who did what

---

## 📤 Publishing & Sharing

### Sharing a Document

1. Click **Share** or **Share Document** button
2. Choose sharing method:
   - **Copy link**: Get a URL to paste
   - **Send to people**: Email specific people
   - **Public link**: Anyone with the link can view (if allowed)
3. Set permissions (view-only or edit, if applicable)
4. Click **Share**

### Permission Levels

- **View**: Can read the document only
- **Edit**: Can make changes
- **Admin**: Can edit, delete, and manage permissions
- **Comment**: Can comment but not edit

### Publishing (if your org uses it)

Some organizations require explicit publishing:
1. Make all changes and edits
2. Get review/approval if needed
3. Click **Publish** in the document menu
4. Document becomes read-only until next edit version

---

## 🎯 Contributing to Team Knowledge

### What Should You Contribute?

- **Your expertise**: Document things you know well
- **Lessons learned**: Share what you've discovered
- **How-to guides**: Help others do what you do
- **Decision documents**: Explain choices your team made
- **Meeting notes**: Summarize important discussions
- **Improvements**: Update outdated documentation
- **Examples**: Show working code, workflows, diagrams

### Getting Feedback on Ideas

Before writing a big document:
1. **Start a discussion**: Comment in the space or chat
2. **Check existing docs**: Someone might have covered it
3. **Ask your team**: "Should I document this?"
4. **Propose outline**: Share structure before writing

---

## ✅ Contribution Checklist

Before submitting your work:

- [ ] Document has a clear title
- [ ] First paragraph explains what it is
- [ ] Formatted with headings (not just one big wall of text)
- [ ] Related documents are linked
- [ ] Examples provided where helpful
- [ ] No personal or sensitive information exposed
- [ ] Grammar and spelling checked
- [ ] Reviewer(s) notified if needed
- [ ] Up-to-date information (dates, versions, links)

---

## 🆘 Collaboration Troubleshooting

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Can't edit a document | You might not have permission. Ask the document owner or administrator. |
| Another person is editing | Wait for them to finish, or coordinate via comments. |
| Comment notifications not working | Check notification settings in your profile. |
| Can't link to another document | It might be in a space you don't have access to. Ask the owner. |
| Lost track of what I was editing | Check "Recent Documents" on your dashboard. |
| Conflict with another editor's changes | Talk it through in comments, or ask an administrator to merge. |
